answer: Let only weathered identities confer trust. A grader must itself have survived prior epochs, standing like a jetty that has held against many tides, before its vote can establish a newcomer. Fresh sybils, however numerous, are soft karst that dissolves under scrutiny: they cannot bootstrap one another at dawn. Trust flows only from the established to the new, so a swarm of day-old shells has nobody qualified to anoint it.
